t: Find Indices With Index and Value Difference II — Editorial
o: We need indices i, j with |i-j| >= indexDifference and |nums[i]-nums[j]| >= valueDifference. In Example 1, i=0 (value 5) and j=3 (value 1) satisfy both conditions. In Example 2, indexDifference=0 lets us pick i=j=0. In Example 3, the only pair at distance >=2 is (0,2), but |1-3|=2 < 4, so no answer exists. With n up to 1e5, an O(n^2) pair scan is borderline (~1e10 worst case) and too slow; we want a linear or near-linear method.
k: For each j, any valid partner i must lie in [0, j-indexDifference] or [j+indexDifference, n-1].
To maximize |nums[i]-nums[j]| against a fixed nums[j], only the maximum and minimum values among candidate partners matter.
Maintaining running prefix max/min as you sweep left-to-right gives an O(n) solution.

a.i: Try every ordered pair of indices and check both conditions directly. This is the most intuitive approach and works for small n, but with n up to 1e5 it can be up to ~1e10 checks in the worst case, so it is mainly a correctness baseline.
s: Loop j from i to n-1.
If abs(i-j) >= indexDifference and abs(nums[i]-nums[j]) >= valueDifference, return [i, j].
If no pair is found after all loops, return [-1, -1].
a.t: O(n^2) — all pairs are checked in the worst case.
a.sp: O(1) extra space besides the output.

a.i: Sweep j from left to right. For each j, valid partners on the left side are exactly indices <= j - indexDifference. Among those, if max(prefix) - nums[j] >= valueDifference, take that max's index; else if nums[j] - min(prefix) >= valueDifference, take that min's index. Since only the extreme values matter for maximizing the absolute difference, keeping a running prefix max and min suffices, giving one pass with constant work per element.
s: Initialize bestMaxIdx = bestMinIdx = 0 (best candidates seen so far).
For j from indexDifference to n-1:
Update bestMaxIdx/bestMinIdx using index j - indexDifference (it just became eligible as a left partner).
If nums[bestMaxIdx] - nums[j] >= valueDifference, return [bestMaxIdx, j].
Else if nums[j] - nums[bestMinIdx] >= valueDifference, return [bestMinIdx, j]. After the loop return [-1, -1].
a.t: O(n) — single pass over the array with O(1) work per element.
a.sp: O(1) extra space besides the output.

w: In an interview, mention brute force briefly to establish the baseline, then present the prefix max/min sweep as the intended O(n) solution. Key pitfalls: when indexDifference = 0, i may equal j (the sweep handles this since j starts at indexDifference); remember to add index j - indexDifference to the candidate pool *before* checking pair (j-indexDifference, j); use 64-bit arithmetic in C++/Java when subtracting values up to 1e9 to avoid overflow concerns. Edge cases: n = 1 with indexDifference = 0 returns [0, 0]; large indexDifference makes the loop body never execute, returning [-1, -1]. Follow-ups might ask for all valid pairs (still O(n) per pair via the same extremes) or handling streaming input (maintain running extremes online).
